title: Immune receptor blocking may reverse aging in mice
summary: Stanford Medicine researchers found that blocking a single immune receptor on tissue-resident macrophages restored their ability to clear senescent neutrophils, reducing inflammation and maintaining youthful function across multiple organs in aged mice. takeaways: Blocking single immune receptor restored cellular cleanup in tissue macrophages
Effects observed across brain, heart, skeletal muscle, liver, spleen, kidney, and colon
Protected mice from frailty, excess fat, and heart trouble
Substantially reduced cognitive decline in aged mice
Published in Science with Katrin Andreasson as senior author

title: Vesper bats possess unique dual antibody gene system enabling virus tolerance
summary: Scientists at Tulane University discovered that over 500 species of vesper bats possess two separate sets of antibody genes, an arrangement never before found in any mammal. takeaways: Over 500 vesper bat species carry dual antibody gene systems

May enable wider antibody variety for viral tolerance
Published in Science Advances on September 3, 2026
Led by Hannah Frank at Tulane University

title: Alzheimer's brain changes detected years before amyloid plaques appear
summary: A 20-year longitudinal study of healthy older adults found structural brain changes occurring at least seven years before amyloid plaques become detectable by PET scans. takeaways: Structural brain changes detected 7+ years before amyloid plaques appear

title: Human-specific gene enables extended brain development and cognitive complexity

Hypothesis: slow maturation contributes to brain's cognitive complexity

sources.label: ScienceDaily / The Zuckerman Institute at Columbia University

title: Liver Regeneration Blocked After Alcohol Use Halts

takeaways: Six patients with treatment-refractory rheumatoid arthritis

title: Seattle scientists launch $95 million AI biology research initiative

takeaways: Mimrylo is a weekly injection
